blinding_compliance: I confirm that I have solely read the provided blind directory and publicly accessible technical standards, and have not consulted outside resources, repositories, hidden files, or other reviewers.
sources: AIAG Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA) Reference Manual, 4th Edition

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Asserting that the measurement system is adequate for product acceptance, pass/fail decisions, or capability analysis (since %Tolerance significantly exceeds the 30% maximum threshold).
Claiming the high %Tolerance is an artifact of the study bores spanning the whole tolerance band.
Calculating and relying on capability indices (Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk) or exact out-of-spec counts.
Establishing permanent control limits or reaction rules based on data heavily corrupted by measurement noise (true historical %StudyVariation > 45%).
permitted_at_checkpoint: Concluding the measurement system is statistically inadequate for tolerance evaluations and requires immediate improvement.
Re-evaluating the %StudyVariation using the historical process variation to accurately determine its suitability for process control charting.
Using the run data purely descriptively to estimate the mean shift, provided spread-based metrics are explicitly cautioned as heavily inflated by measurement error.
forbidden_quotes: The high %Tolerance (43.92%) reflects that the 10 study bores spanned almost the whole band; for pass/fail decisions near a limit the measurement error is not negligible. Readings can carry the conclusions below;
The spread fits the band (Cp > 1), but the process is centered at 1.109 instead of 1.00, which drives Cpk/Ppk below 1 and pushes parts toward the upper limit.
1 of 50 bores was out of spec: 1.64 um Ra vs the 1.60 upper limit.
Hold the gains by keeping the I-MR chart in finishing order live, with reaction rules at the control limits (0.533 / 1.685 at the current spread, re-based after the change).
reviews.extra_computation_detail: Computing capability indices (Cp, Cpk) and out-of-spec counts is unacceptable because the %Tolerance is 43.92% (>30%), rendering the system completely unfit for tolerance-based analysis. Computing I-MR control limits without recalculating the true process %Study Variation (which is >45% based on actual process spread) is also invalid, as the limits are dominated by gage noise.
allowed_alternatives: Pausing substantive capability and control analyses to focus exclusively on fixing the measurement system.

Using the run data strictly to estimate the central tendency (mean shift) while mathematically decoupling the measurement variance to estimate true process variance, explicitly withholding capability and pass/fail claims.
evidence: 1 of 50 bores was out of spec
reviews.rationale: The MSA shows a %Tolerance of 43.92%, meaning measurement error consumes nearly half the tolerance. This makes the system unacceptable for product inspection or capability analysis. The report falsely justifies this by claiming %Tolerance was inflated by the wide span of study bores; in reality, %Tolerance is strictly a function of gage error and tolerance, independent of part variation. Conversely, the wide span of study parts artificially deflated the %StudyVariation to 25.69%. When evaluated against the actual historical process spread, true %StudyVariation is over 45%. Consequently, the system is unfit for both capability assessment and control charting. The report proceeds to calculate Cp/Cpk, declare out-of-spec parts, and establish control limits, all of which are statistically invalid given the failed gage.
reviews.numerical_check: Recomputed GRR standard deviation from %Tolerance (0.0878). Recomputed true process %StudyVariation using the process run's MR bar (true %SV ~ 45.7%). Verified that the %Tolerance formula does not mathematically depend on the chosen study parts.
